prompts.content:
Where the Wing Remembers Both Shores

The dragon does not choose a century.
It is the century choosing itself
through a body made of postponement and afterglow.
One wing trails the last unburned page of a library
that fell before paper learned its own name.
The other combs holographic rain
from towers that have not yet decided
whether they will stand or become rumor.
Between them the air keeps two calendars
and forgets which one is running.
Its scales are older than the word for scale.
They remember the heat of forges
that have not been lit,
and the cold of stars
that have already gone out
in some other telling.
Runes surface and sink like thoughts
a city has not earned the right to think.
Each pulse of light is both relic and prototype.
Below, the streets are wet with what has happened
and what is still negotiating its arrival.
Neon writes on water that was once a glacier’s patience
and will be, later, only a rumor of thirst.
Foundations rest on the quiet of forests
that still dream they are standing.
Billboards advertise tomorrows
already homesick for the dusk that has not come.
The creature’s eyes hold the only honest weather:
one the green of a memory
that does not yet know it is finished,
the other the blue of a question
that has not found the mouth that will ask it.
They look at us the way time looks at itself
when no one is watching
without pity, without verdict,
only the long courtesy of attention.
We live in the brief downdraft of its passing,
that strange, merciful interval
where the past is still unfinished with us
and the future has already begun
to miss what we have not yet lost.
Nothing is promised except the turning:	he slow, luminous hinge of a wing
that belongs to every hour at once
and to none of them completely.
The mist it leaves is neither ending nor beginning.
It is the place they briefly recognize each other
before the next uncertainty
opens its quiet, necessary hand.

prompts.title: High-Fashion Editorial Prompt
prompts.description: A detailed prompt for generating a high-fashion editorial image featuring a woman seated by a lake with red flowers, designed for Nano Banana 2 (likely compatible with Pro).
prompts.content: Create a vertical high-fashion editorial at an outdoor formal dining table beside a calm lake or reflecting water, photographed in clear directional daylight with dense red flowers surrounding the subject at multiple depths. Frame an adult woman seated beside a long ivory-covered table, approximately from the knees to above the head. Keep the composition asymmetrical: let a large mass of deep crimson flowers dominate the left side and additional blurred red blooms enter very close to camera across the lower foreground, partially interrupting the table and lower body. Preserve enough open background behind the woman to reveal softly defocused water, dark green foliage and muted autumnal trees without turning the location into a scenic landscape portrait. Build the pose around stillness rather than active dining. Let one elbow rest naturally on the table edge while the corresponding hand supports the side of the face near the cheek and jaw. Keep the wrist relaxed rather than posed delicately. Let the opposite arm fall low beside the body or rest loosely across the lap. The torso remains upright but slightly settled into one hip, with the shoulders uneven and relaxed. Turn the face only slightly toward camera while the gaze drifts just past it. Keep the expression composed, detached and faintly impatient rather than romantic, smiling or dreamy. The mouth should stay relaxed but defined by a strong deep-crimson lip. Dress her in a long oversized emerald-green coat with broad lapels, substantial shoulders and dense matte wool or cashmere texture. Let the coat hang open and wrap heavily around the arms and sides without appearing tailored too tightly to the body. Underneath, reveal a fluid ivory silk-satin dress with a softly draped neckline and long skirt falling in broad luminous folds over the seated legs. The coat should absorb light while the dress catches long soft highlights, creating a clear material contrast. Style the hair sleek, dark and close to the head with a precise deep side part, pulled into a compact low bun or smooth gathered shape so the face, neck and earrings remain unobstructed. Add oversized crystal or pavé drop earrings built from two stacked oval or teardrop forms, substantial enough to remain visible against the dark coat and hair. Keep other jewelry minimal or absent so the earrings remain the only sharp metallic sparkle near the face. Construct the flowers as dense arrangements of dark-red roses, carnations, ranunculus and similarly ruffled blooms rather than one repeated flower type. Use varying scales, imperfect petal shapes and occasional dark green stems or leaves. Keep the red masses rich and dimensional rather than bright scarlet or bridal pastel. Include only restrained table details: an ivory textured cloth, one or two clear cut-crystal glasses, subtle silverware and perhaps a few understated plates partially obscured by flowers.
